supersedes: transpositions_2014-07.npz (v1) -- v1 REMAINS PUBLISHED AND UNCHANGED; v2 is a strict superset: all 13 v1 data columns plus `meta` are BIT-IDENTICAL, in the same row order, and four columns are APPENDED.
why_v2: v1 failed i4's own validate_contract(): it requires state_hash128_lo, state_hash128_hi, player_hash, player_fold, none of which v1 contained, so i4's player-disjoint primary scoring and its 128-bit collision audit were both unrunnable. That was an omission in the extraction brief, not a thread-side change.

scope.rule: one record per ply p with MIN_PLY <= p < MAX_PLY and at least 4 preceding plies; the record describes the position BEFORE the move stored in nxt. Emitted ply values are 6..29 INCLUSIVE. Ply 30 is NOT emitted.

ply30_inclusive_would_add.current_build: MAX_PLY=30 EXCLUSIVE -- records at ply 6..29 inclusive; ply 30 IS NOT INCLUDED
ply30_inclusive_would_add.definition: exactly the number of games that have a move at 0-based ply index 30 (i.e. mainline length >= 31); each would emit one extra record

hashing.int64_encoding: int.from_bytes(digest, 'little', signed=True) -- SIGNED int64 for every digest column. Reinterpret as unsigned at zero cost with .view(np.uint64).
hashing.note: state_fen5/hist1/hist4/nxt use blake2b(digest_size=8) with NO personalization, bit-identical to the pass-1 scout extraction and to v1.

repetition_ledger_spec_as_implemented.ledger_key_k: python-chess Board.epd() = placement / side-to-move / castling / LEGAL en-passant. Library call: chess.Board.epd() with its default en_passant='legal' (verified equal to ' '.join(board.fen().split(' ')[:4])). halfmove and fullmove counters are EXCLUDED.
repetition_ledger_spec_as_implemented.segment_reset: chess.Board.is_irreversible(move) evaluated on the PRE-move board (is_zeroing OR _reduces_castling_rights OR has_legal_en_passant). After an irreversible move the count-map is cleared and re-seeded with the post-move position at count 1.
repetition_ledger_spec_as_implemented.count_map: {k: occurrences} over the current reversible segment, INCLUDING the current position; seeded at the game's initial position with count 1.
repetition_ledger_spec_as_implemented.serialization: '\n'.join('<k>:<count>') over items in LEXICOGRAPHIC KEY ORDER (python sorted() on the ASCII EPD strings), encoded UTF-8.
repetition_ledger_spec_as_implemented.X_t: state = blake2b(fen_fields_1to5.encode('utf-8') || L_t_RAW_8_BYTES, digest_size=8, person=b'i4-rep-v1').  The concatenation uses the 8 RAW digest bytes of L_t (not hex, not decimal). fen_fields_1to5 is the space-joined first five FEN fields.

V2_NEW_COLUMNS_LITERAL_READINGS.STATUS: i4's spec was SILENT on all five points below. We implemented the most literal, most obvious reading of each and RAN, rather than idling the lane for a ~20-minute round trip. EVERY ONE IS A ONE-LINE RECOMPUTE OR A ~7-MINUTE RE-EXTRACTION. Correct any you dislike.

1_player_hash_digest_params.why: the same convention the repetition ledger already uses; NOT the unpersonalized h64() used by the pass-1-compatible columns, because player identity is new in this pass and has no pass-1 bench to stay bit-compatible with
1_player_hash_digest_params.identity_string: the PGN White/Black tag VERBATIM -- no casefold, no strip, no unicode normalisation. python-chess supplies '?' when the tag is absent.
1_player_hash_digest_params.which_player: the MOVER: the side to move in the position the record describes, i.e. the player who plays the move stored in `nxt`. Taken from chess.Board.turn (WHITE -> 'White' tag, BLACK -> 'Black' tag), NOT from ply parity arithmetic.

2_player_fold_splitmix64_constants.chosen: player_fold = player_hash & 1  -- the LOW BIT of the 64-bit digest. NO splitmix64 mixing step, no constants.
2_player_fold_splitmix64_constants.why: blake2b output is already uniform, so its low bit is an unbiased fair coin; adding splitmix64 constants would be a second undocumented choice with no benefit
2_player_fold_splitmix64_constants.disjointness: fold is a PURE FUNCTION of player_hash, so no mover can appear in both folds. Disjointness is by construction, and was verified on every record.
2_player_fold_splitmix64_constants.recompute_cost: ZERO re-extraction -- player_hash is in the file, so any alternative fold rule (splitmix64, top bit, k-way, stratified) is one line in your sandbox

3_128bit_personalization_and_which_half_.input_bytes: IDENTICAL to the `state` column: fen_fields_1to5.encode('utf-8') || L_t_RAW_8_BYTES
3_128bit_personalization_and_which_half_.chosen: d16 = blake2b(x_in, digest_size=16, person=b'i4-rep-v1').digest(); state_hash128_lo = int.from_bytes(d16[0:8], 'little', signed=True); state_hash128_hi = int.from_bytes(d16[8:16], 'little', signed=True)
3_128bit_personalization_and_which_half_.lo_is: the FIRST eight digest bytes, little-endian -- matching the existing little-endian int64 encoding used for every other digest column
3_128bit_personalization_and_which_half_.READ_THIS: blake2b folds digest_size into its parameter block, so the 16-byte digest is NOT an extension of the 8-byte one: state != state_hash128_lo on every record. They are two INDEPENDENT hashes of the SAME input bytes. That is exactly what makes the collision audit valid -- equal 128-bit pair => equal input => equal 64-bit state, so any group sharing `state` but not (lo,hi) is a genuine 64-bit collision.

4_ply_30_inclusive_or_exclusive.chosen: EXCLUSIVE -- unchanged from v1. Records are emitted at ply 6..29; PLY 30 IS ABSENT.
4_ply_30_inclusive_or_exclusive.why: changing it would break bit-identity with v1, which was the other hard requirement. Measured instead, exactly.

measured.current_build: MAX_PLY=30 EXCLUSIVE -- records at ply 6..29 inclusive; ply 30 IS NOT INCLUDED
measured.definition: exactly the number of games that have a move at 0-based ply index 30 (i.e. mainline length >= 31); each would emit one extra record

5_dtype_signedness.chosen: SIGNED int64 for state_hash128_lo, state_hash128_hi and player_hash (int.from_bytes(..., 'little', signed=True)), matching every existing digest column in v1. player_fold is uint8 with values {0,1}.

state.meaning: X_t, the RULE-COMPLETE state key (FEN 1-5 + repetition ledger)

state_fen5.meaning: pass-1 scout key: hash of FEN fields 1-5 only, rule-INCOMPLETE; carried so the scout-vs-complete re-partition is measurable in-file

hist1.meaning: hash of the single preceding move (UCI)

hist4.meaning: hash of the 4 preceding moves, space-joined UCI, oldest first

nxt.meaning: hash of the move actually played from this state (UCI) -- the prediction target

gidx.meaning: game index, 0..n_games-1, globally unique and non-decreasing; use for game-disjoint train/held-out splits

tclass.meaning: time control from base+40*inc: 0 bullet <179s, 1 blitz <479s, 2 rapid <1499s, 3 classical; -1 unknown

current_position_occurrence_count.meaning: count-map[k_current], >=1, INCLUDES the current occurrence; saturates at 255

can_claim_threefold_now.meaning: current position has occurred >=3 times in the segment. NOT python-chess can_claim_threefold_repetition(), which also returns True for the after-one-move case

can_claim_threefold_after_one_move.meaning: exists a legal move whose resulting position has occurred 3 times; reported INDEPENDENTLY of can_claim_threefold_now

meta.meaning: [n_games, n_records, MIN_PLY, MAX_PLY, variant_games_skipped, n_legalmove_scans] -- BIT-IDENTICAL to v1

state_hash128_lo.meaning: low 64 bits (first 8 digest bytes, little-endian, signed) of the 128-bit blake2b of the SAME input as `state`

state_hash128_hi.meaning: high 64 bits (last 8 digest bytes, little-endian, signed) of the same 128-bit digest. (lo,hi) together are the collision-audit reference key.

player_hash.meaning: blake2b-64(person='i4-rep-v1') of the MOVER's PGN username, verbatim. The mover is the side to move, i.e. whoever plays `nxt`.

player_fold.meaning: player_hash & 1, in {0,1}. Player-disjoint 2-way split: a mover is in exactly one fold BY CONSTRUCTION. NOTE this is not game-disjoint -- a game whose two players fold differently contributes to both folds. Use gidx for game-disjoint splits.

meta2.meaning: [n_games_with_a_move_at_ply_index_30, -1]. meta2[0] is exactly the number of extra records a ply-30-INCLUSIVE build would emit. meta2[1] is a placeholder (-1): per-chunk distinct-name counts are not globally unique; the global distinct-mover count is in verification.player_disjoint_split.

not_computed_here: No estimator, no delta_1/2/3/4, no verdict, no permutation test. i4 owns the estimator spec and has now shipped its own source; building a second one risks a silently different statistic.

verification.eight_way_split_byte_exact: chunk bytes sum to 1048308056 == decompressed original; every chunk starts on a '[Event "' game boundary
verification.split_count_is_irrelevant_to_output: v1 used 6 chunks, v2 used 8. The merged arrays are independent of the chunking: chunks partition the game stream in order and gidx offsets accumulate, so the concatenation is identical either way -- as the bit-identity check below confirms on the full corpus.
verification.PREFLIGHT_bit_identity_20k_games: on the first 20,000 games (458,108 records) all 13 v1 columns matched the v1 file AND the original pass-2 bench, bit for bit, BEFORE the full run was launched

FULL_CORPUS_bit_identity_vs_v1.scope: FULL CORPUS, every record (not a slice)

collision_audit_64bit.method: equal 128-bit pair => equal input => equal 64-bit state, so D128 - D64 is exactly the number of distinct rule-complete states that a 64-bit key merges away

player_disjoint_split.note: fold is a pure function of player_hash, so a mover is in exactly one fold BY CONSTRUCTION. A GAME however contributes to both folds whenever its two players fold differently -- player-disjointness is at the MOVER level, and it is NOT game-disjoint. Both are available: gidx for game-disjoint, player_fold for player-disjoint.
player_disjoint_split.READ_THIS: The mover pool for this whole corpus is only 30,350 distinct usernames across 1,048,440 games -- median 96 records per mover, max 49,867. A 2-way player-disjoint split is therefore coarse: each fold holds ~15,000 movers, and a single heavy user can carry ~0.2% of a fold's records. If your '>=2 movers per history class' eligibility rule is tight, check it against this pool size before scoring.

identity_string_normalisation.choice: PGN tag hashed VERBATIM (no casefold / strip / normalise) -- the literal reading

repetition_rarity_in_this_ply_window.READ_THIS: Within MIN_PLY=6..MAX_PLY=30 actual repetitions are near-absent. The rule-completeness fix therefore bites almost entirely through SEGMENT MEMBERSHIP (which reversible positions preceded this one), not through realised repetitions. The two threefold-claim columns are near-degenerate at this window; to make repetition RIGHTS a live discriminator the ply window must extend well past 30.

ledger_hand_checks: knight-shuffle threefold -> current_position_occurrence_count == 3, agrees with python-chess Board.is_repetition(3)
an intervening pawn move resets the segment -> count 2, not 3
a legal en-passant makes every move irreversible (is_irreversible True for a quiet knight move)

run.v1_comparison: v1 was 443.68 s on 6 workers; v2 is 346.3 s on 8 workers despite the extra 128-bit digest and per-record player columns
